summary: A trim records its tombstones in 20 ms chunks instead of one long transaction

schema.detail: No tables, columns or indexes. The checkpoints table gains a 'recording' state value while a trim records its tombstones.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged; the same claims are dropped. A sealed set ignores tombstones of a checkpoint still recording, so a node interrupted mid-recording plans the same drop and verifies the same certificate.

compatibility.detail: Inventories, authority digests and manifests are unchanged: a tombstone and its envelope share one identity, and manifests read tombstones by checkpoint name. Adoption of a peer's manifest still records in one transaction, as it replaces every other tombstone.

downtime.detail: None. On a production copy, a 468,134-claim trim held the writer at p50 41 ms / p99 229 ms instead of a single 53 s transaction.

recovery.detail: An older build that finds a checkpoint in the 'recording' state after a rollback treats it as not applied: its sealed set then reads the partial tombstones, its plan differs from the certificate, and it adopts the manifest from a peer, which replaces those tombstones. Roll back only after a trim finishes, or expect one manifest adoption.
